svg.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: How Datapipe makes a Short
svg.text: uv run datapipe short <method> <input>: read the audio, render headless in Blender, encode and check. One command, no post-production.
Committed recipes · look.toml is the schema
config/pipeline.toml picks the look per method
opens a run · Save to run
· H.264 High, BT.709 tags, index first
· true peak ≤ −1 dBTP; A at −14 LUFS
· hits of the light ring's track in sync
· loop seam: frame n + 1 matches frame 1
Drop a master, stems or MIDI into inbox/<method>/; the method decides how the audio is read.
song/ decodes every file to 48 kHz, checks they line up, and finds hits, tempo and sections.
Method A needs no file: gen/ composes a score and renders an 8-second loop with DawDreamer.
Every method writes the same run folder: mix.wav plus controls.json, one schema for all six.
Headless Blender reads controls.json; mapping.py bakes it into per-frame look signals.
The method's mapping says which sound drives what; the style sets the tunnel's shape and look.
EEVEE renders the neon tunnel to PNG frames, 1080×1920 at 60 fps (S5).
PyAV encodes the frames and mix.wav to H.264 and AAC for YouTube (S6).
S7 checks format, length, loudness, sync, the loop seam and flashes, then fills output/<method>/.
Optional: datapipe tune opens a run in Blender; save it to the run, or as the method's default.
